seal.statement: Amendment 4's two-file closed shape is replaced by a minimal-terminal-proof shape. A closed quest holds its canonical record, its append-only log, and exactly those proof artifacts its sealed terminal claim requires; anything else is rejected, and a required artifact may be neither deleted nor modified after closure. Which artifacts a sealed doneWhen requires is answered structurally by the probe owner, never inferred from prose or a filename, so naming a file in text cannot legalize it. Retained proof stays counted in the active footprint.

text: Amendment 4 revised prospectively. scripts/solve/probes.js gains requiredProofArtifacts(doneWhen): the probe owner answers which repository paths a sealed claim designates, since it owns how each kind is measured (test-receipt and oracle name a file; scenario-harness and script retain nothing). scripts/checks/check-closed-quest-shape.js compares a closed quest's contents against {quest.json, log.ndjson} union those artifacts, and refuses post-closure mutation across admitted commit transitions, so deletion being illegal does not leave rewriting free. Git transition machinery moved to scripts/checks/quest-record-transitions.js and is now shared with the append-only audit rather than duplicated. The budget's shape row defers to the new owner instead of restating the rule, and the audit is registered in test:static. No quest id appears anywhere in the implementation: the two landed quests are admitted by the general rule from their own sealed claims.
